No, we can't certify that. The evidence shows that NASA FIRMS recorded zero thermal detections intersecting the asset (ASSET-F06) between 2026-10-06 and 2026-11-05. All four sensors (VIIRS S-NPP, NOAA-20, NOAA-21 and MODIS) covered every day of that period, so the absence of detections is a well-observed result.

However, "not detected" is not the same as "no fire occurred." Small, short-lived, cool or cloud-obscured fires can go undetected at 375 m (VIIRS) or 1 km (MODIS) resolution. The evidence also says nothing about burned area, the cause of any land change, or anything outside this period.

A defensible statement would be: "No FIRMS thermal anomalies were detected on the asset during 2026-10-06 to 2026-11-05, with full sensor coverage." If you need stronger assurance, you would need additional evidence such as burned-area analysis, high-resolution imagery, or a site report.
